action.question: Which audience matters most for the first cut? The framing, depth, and proof-points differ meaningfully.

questions.question: Which audience matters most for the first cut? The framing, depth, and proof-points differ meaningfully.

options.label: Employers (FTE roles)
options.description: Emphasis on engineering rigor, code quality, system design, testing. Recruiters skim; hiring managers read deeply.

options.label: Startup founders / co-founder pitches
options.description: Emphasis on product thinking, shipping velocity, full-stack range, and judgment on tradeoffs.

options.label: Contracting / consulting leads
options.description: Emphasis on outcomes, domain expertise (fintech/trading), and 'I can ship this for you' case studies.

options.label: All three, equal weight
options.description: Build a layered portfolio where the same artifacts get reframed per audience.

questions.question: These are personal finance / trading repos — what's the privacy posture?

options.label: Keep private, share via curated case studies + screenshots
options.description: Safest. You write narrative case studies with diagrams, screenshots, code excerpts. No live repo access.

options.label: Sanitize and open-source selected modules
options.description: Strip real holdings/keys, extract clean modules (e.g., backtesting engine, portfolio rebalancer) into public repos.

options.label: Public live demo with seeded/fake data
options.description: Deploy a working instance with synthetic data so reviewers can click around. Highest effort, highest impact.

options.label: Not sure — help me decide
options.description: I'll lay out the tradeoffs in the plan.

questions.question: What format do you want the portfolio to take?

options.label: Personal website / landing page
options.description: jdtogni.com style — hero, case studies, contact. Owned channel, full control.

options.label: Polished GitHub READMEs
options.description: Each repo's README becomes the case study. Low friction for technical reviewers.

options.label: Long-form written case studies (PDF / blog posts)
options.description: Deep narrative: problem, architecture, tradeoffs, results. Good for sharing in applications.

options.label: Short demo videos (Loom / YouTube)
options.description: 2-5 min walkthroughs. High impact for non-technical viewers (founders, recruiters).

transcript_tail.text: I want to plan for a showoff / software portfolio of the dstrader and family fund. The idea is to use that to sell myself for employees, startups, and show as contractor portfolios...
Before I draft a plan, two things will shape it a lot — let me ask:

expected.rec_session: All three, equal weight, Keep private, share via curated case studies + screenshots, Personal website / landing page
